The modules used here were added in three steps: \texttt{Ownership}, \texttt{Theory}, \texttt{A0Numeric} and \texttt{DoorEleven} (47 theorems, 219 in the library), \texttt{Action}, \texttt{Dimension} and \texttt{FluidLink} (62 theorems, 281), and \texttt{CalibrationWall} (50 theorems, 331).
\emph{Lean certifies implications from premises, not data.} $\kappa=\tfrac12$, the kernel, $\rho_\Lambda$ constant, the hierarchy and the ownership rule enter as named premises.

\item \textbf{Ownership is non-local.} If $\nu\ne1$, a top-level and an owned system with the same internal and external fields get different internal accelerations, so no function of the field data reproduces the rule (\texttt{ownership\_distinguishes}, \texttt{ownership\_not\_field\_local}); B's own kernel meets the premise (\texttt{CandidateB.ownership\_nonlocal}).

\item \textbf{No external-field effect forces linearity.} A continuous map with $F(z+z_e)-F(z_e)=F(z)$ is linear (\texttt{noEFE\_continuousLinear}); hence no pointwise law with MOND's deep limit is EFE-free, in scalar or vector form (\texttt{law\_not\_efeFreeRay}, \texttt{vecLaw\_not\_efeFree}).
This covers pointwise (QUMOND-type) laws only, not the AQUAL or QUMOND field equations.
Ownership escapes only because it is non-local.
\item \textbf{The dimension theorem.} No monomial in $(G,M,c)$ is a length $\propto M^{1/2}$; with one extra constant $X$ such a length exists if and only if $(G,c,X)$ form an acceleration scale.
What is forced is an acceleration scale, not that $X$ is an acceleration ($\hbar$ is admissible).
Monomials only.

\item \textbf{The AQUAL action gives the kernel.} For an AQUAL $\mu$ with $x\mu(x)$ increasing onto $(0,\infty)$, the spherical Gauss form $\mu(g/a_0)g=g_N$ is equivalent to $g=\nu(g_N/a_0)g_N$, and P2's kernel follows from $\mu=(\sqrt{1+4x^2}-1)/(2x)$.
Premises: the reduced Euler--Lagrange equation and regularity; spherical symmetry only.
Ownership and the cold-mass rule stay postulates.

\item \textbf{The calibration wall (CFG240).} In the deep limit $g_{\rm obs}$ depends only on $f\cdot a_0$ ($f$ a baryon calibration); for exact P2 two distinct $g_{\rm bar}$ identify $(f,a_0)$; with $f$ free, $\sigma(\log a_0)\ge3\sigma/\sqrt N$ (conditional on local slopes in $[0,\tfrac12]$).
These are the theorems behind PAPER38 [P38].

text: Each item is a necessary condition read off the failures of scored classes; none is shown sufficient, and the set is not shown jointly satisfiable.
CFG230 lists twelve requirements of the same kind (R01--R12) and finds that only R01 and R02 are met by any scored row as a mechanism.
\item \textbf{An early cold fluid, present before structure.} The fluid must exist with the cosmic amount at recombination.

A conserved dust created at turnaround supplies $\Omega h^2=0.1200\times10^{-1376.8}$ at $z=1100$, and in a baryon-only universe the trigger never fires (CFG243; the baryon-only $\sigma_b$ is 0.076 against the threshold 1.276).
A turnaround source can at most add to or relabel the early fluid.
Continuous vacuum-to-fluid transfer after recombination can make only a few per cent of it (CFG253).
The premise of the conservation rule [P36] is exactly what such classes cannot supply.

\item \textbf{Ownership that remembers boundness, on that early fluid.} A causal doubled-field latch passes causality and bound-only rows but forgets a static bound system ($n(t_{\rm ff})=0.791$ against 0.99); a post-hoc energy-driven repair needs 5.0 free-fall times and an untied coupling (CFG242).
A first-crossing rule gives ownership to the smallest progenitors: only 0.16--0.21 of the baryons first turn around in a system of at least 0.1 of the final mass (CFG243, post hoc).
Ownership is not field-local (Lean, Section~\ref{sec:lean}).
\item \textbf{A distribution that carries the $M^{1/2}$ acceleration scale itself.} By the dimension theorem an acceleration scale must enter.

Passive infall does not supply it ($M^{0.33}$; CFG118, CFG244), and a relaxation at a vacuum-set rate is too slow: the 10\% line needs $\Gamma\ge$ 5.37 / 5.17 $H_\Lambda$ (can/alt) at $\tau=t_0$, and partial relaxation misses the RAR by 0.15--0.28 dex against the 0.10 line (CFG245).
The galaxy and cluster windows nearly meet near 1.7--1.9 $H_\Lambda$, a rate no vacuum candidate provides (arithmetic, not a finding).

\item \textbf{Field-local in the Newtonian field, but labelled by bound domains.} The law's local-field (QUMOND phantom) density is a function of the Newtonian field, but it is not the CFG44 target for extended baryons (ratio up to 2.33 for P2), and the local form does not give ownership (internal-to-Newtonian ratio up to 3.16 where ownership needs 1): the local target needs non-local labels, a bound domain and a supply cap (CFG245, G0).

\item \textbf{No created rest mass.} The heat ledger is not the obstacle (at most 1.9e-4 of the vacuum energy of the ball, CFG242), but for any class that creates rest mass the ledger is: $f(30)=24.8$ in one $r_{\rm ta}$ convention, and 1.7 against 1 on the Lagrangian-volume ledger (CFG243, CFG131).

\item \textbf{The inherited gates.} Cold at $z\gtrsim10$ to $k=30$/Mpc ($c_s^2\le$ 4.608e-12, CFG230 R05); reaction and energy within G3 (exchange forms give 22.5 $g_{\rm law}$, CFG242); no new constant (G4); an external-field branch chosen explicitly (ownership, or an EFE that DR4 can see); and a Solar tail handled by ownership or by screening $\ge$ 3.5e3 for any kernel with a tail $\ge$ 0.28205 $a_0$ (CFG230 R09).

In one sentence: the target is an early cold fluid with the cosmic amount, owned by a memory-carrying, bound-domain assignment, whose distribution carries the $M^{1/2}$ scale itself; neither passive infall nor vacuum-rate relaxation supplies it, and no committed construction derives it.
\textbf{The failure.} Under ownership an accreted satellite obeys the isolated law of its infall baryons.

For the Milky Way ultra-faints that law under-predicts the dispersions: the Kaplan--Meier median offset is $+0.3245\pm0.038$ (3.77$\sigma$, canonical) with the nine upper limits restored and a 0.077-dex systematic floor (CFG28); tides and noise do not explain it, and the published binary bounds do not either (CFG29).
The $\Lambda$CDM side is weakly diagnostic here: its pass window spans 3.5--5 decades of halo mass.

\textbf{The 2026 dispersions (CFG259).} Re-scoring with the DEIMOS archive [G26] and the binary corrections of [AP26] moves B's median by at most 0.005 dex; the significance stays 3.5 to 3.9$\sigma$ on both footings.
The corrections reach 8 of 40 systems, with a median of $-0.068$ dex (free binary fraction) or $-0.104$ dex ($f=0.7$), a fifth to a third of the offset.
The one place they bite is CFG29's weak-binary subsample, which drops to 2.8$\sigma$ / 2.6$\sigma$ under the $f=0.7$ correction.
The Bo\"otes~I conflict between the multi-epoch value and the single-epoch correction changes none of this.
